pc_new: DSPM discovers data on AWS, Azure, GCP, Snowflake, Microsoft 365 and on-prem file shares
quote: Prisma Cloud offers data classification for the following assets and services.
notes: Supported assets: AWS (S3, EFS, Aurora, RDS, OpenSearch Serverless, DynamoDB, Redshift, EC2-hosted DBs), Azure (Blob, NetApp Files, SQL, CosmosDB), GCP (Cloud Storage, BigTable, Cloud SQL, BigQuery), Snowflake, M365 OneDrive/SharePoint, unmanaged DBs on VMs. On-prem: Windows file shares only, over internet or peering to a cloud-hosted orchestrator (https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/data-security-posture-management/prisma-cloud-dspm-deployment/file-shares/on-premise-file-shares, 'Presently, only the Windows file system is supported.'). Live cell names the 'Data Security' module. That module (PCDS) went End of Sale on Aug 31 2024 and DSPM replaced it (release notes Aug 2024). DSPM is a separate subscription in EE, metered per data asset.

pc_new: Predefined and custom classifiers for structured and unstructured data, mapped to HIPAA, GDPR, PCI
quote: Classification is performed via Prisma Cloud DSPMs proprietary engine, which includes pre-defined classifiers with contextual capabilities for minimizing the false-positive rate.
notes: Also: 'Clients can also add their own customized classifiers.' Regulation mapping: https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/data-security-posture-management/data-security-posture-management ('classify data under these regulations', HIPAA, GDPR, PCI). A '100+ classifiers' figure appears in search snippets of an older DSPM page that now returns 404, so it is not used here.

pc_new: Access tab maps users and roles with Read, Write, List, Manage and public access
quote: The access information shows all users and roles who have access to the data asset scope, including access levels (e.g. Read, Write, List and Manage) and public access
notes: Requires both DSPM and CIEM subscriptions: 'the tenant needs to be subscribed both to DSPM and CIEM.' Covers AWS S3, RDS, EFS, Aurora, OpenSearch, DynamoDB; Azure Storage, NetApp, SQL, CosmosDB; GCP GCS, BigTable, CloudSQL, BigQuery. DDR adds near-real-time activity monitoring (under 15 min) from CloudTrail and Activity Logs.

pc_new: DSPM shows public access on data assets and flags exposure through risk rules
quote: The access information shows all users and roles who have access to the data asset scope, including access levels (e.g. Read, Write, List and Manage) and public access
notes: Custom risk example in docs: 'developer secrets that are open to the world' (https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/data-security-posture-management/how-to-articles/create-and-edit-custom-risks). Access data depends on the CIEM subscription.

pc_new: Built-in and custom DSPM risk rules plus DDR policies raise alerts on data assets
quote: Create custom risk rules from any search in the inventory and save them.
notes: DDR policy categories: First Move, Attack, Compliance (https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/data-security-posture-management/welcome/platform-overview/ddr-policies). Controls are detective (risk findings and alerts). Remediation runs through integrations such as XSOAR, Jira, Slack, webhooks. The DSPM section documents no inline blocking.

pc_new: Built-in list names 60+ standards for AWS, plus Azure, GCP, Alibaba, OCI and custom
quote: The built-in regulatory compliance standards that Prisma Cloud supports are listed in the following table.
notes: Table counts (items as listed, some duplicates): AWS 67, Azure 54, GCP 51, Alibaba 40, OCI 32, about 89 distinct names overall. Includes PCI DSS v4.0, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001:2022, NIST 800-53 Rev5, FedRAMP Moderate/Low, APRA CPS 234, CIS. The table lags the release notes: 2025-2026 notes add FedRAMP High, CIS AWS v4-v6, CIS Azure v3-v5, CIS GCP v4, TISAX, NCSC, CSAP, AESCSF v2. DSPM has its own compliance page (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53).

pc_new: One-time or recurring compliance reports per standard, filtered by account and region, emailed
quote: Create reports based on a cloud compliance standard for immediate viewing or download, or schedule recurring reports to continue monitoring compliance over time.
notes: Runtime (Defender) compliance has a separate Compliance Explorer and reports for hosts, containers, serverless. DSPM has a separate compliance page and reports.

pc_new: Alerts send to Jira, Email, Slack, export to CSV, dismiss or snooze with reason
quote: As needed, Download the filtered list of alert details to a CSV file.
notes: Also 'Send to Jira' from the Alert ID. This page describes no free-text comment thread on alerts, only dismiss and snooze reasons and optional messages on Email or Slack send. DSPM has its own Jira, Slack, PagerDuty, Torq and webhook integrations (https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/data-security-posture-management/prisma-cloud-dspm-integrations), which supports the live claim that workflows sit per module.

param: Automated Red Teaming (GenAI / LLMs on AWS, GCP, Azure)
pc_new: Not in Enterprise Edition; AI red teaming is sold as Prisma AIRS
quote: AI-SPM provides risk assessment for the supported AI assets, with risk rules crafted by the Prisma Cloud research team.
notes: All six EE AI-SPM pages read (intro, ecosystem components, overview, onboarding, supported assets, unmanaged models). They cover posture only and no red teaming. Red teaming exists in separately licensed Prisma AIRS AI Red Teaming: https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-runtime-security/ai-red-teaming/identify-ai-system-risks-with-ai-red-teaming/get-started-with-prisma-airs-ai-red-teaming. Live text 'AI security capabilities limited' is editorial, so replace it.

pc_new: Not in Enterprise Edition; prompt inspection is sold as Prisma AIRS runtime security
quote: These risk rules are designed to detect misconfigurations and security flaws in AI assets and alert on them.
notes: The cross icon is correct, but the live text says 'Limited' and contradicts it. EE AI-SPM is posture-only. Runtime prompt protection is in Prisma AIRS (separate license): https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-security/prisma-airs. A Dec 2024 PANW blog says AI-SPM capabilities are augmented with runtime protection tools (https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/cloud-security/ai-application-security-owasp-llm-nist/).

pc_new: AI-SPM finds Hugging Face model files on VMs; file scanning is Prisma AIRS
quote: Prisma Cloud identifies model files on Virtual Machines (VMs).
notes: EE discovers unmanaged models (GPT, Llama, Falcon, Gemma, Mistral and more from Hugging Face) on AWS, Azure and GCP VMs. The docs show no scan for unsafe serialization. Model scanning for deserialization and tampering is Prisma AIRS AI Model Security, separately licensed (https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-security/prisma-airs). Live text 'limited' contradicts the cross icon, so replace it.

pc_new: AI-SPM maps posture findings to OWASP Top 10 for LLM and NIST AI 600-1
quote: Prisma Cloud AISPM now includes enhanced risk identification and compliance capabilities for AI and ML systems that aligns with two critical standards
notes: Release 24.12.1 (Dec 2024). The sentence continues: 'OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Models (LLM) and NIST AI 600-1.' Coverage is posture and compliance mapping, not runtime or prompt enforcement. The cross icon is outdated and a dash fits. Status 'Limited' reflects mapping-only coverage versus AccuKnox runtime enforcement.

pc_new: Generic container and host runtime defense; AI-SPM docs show no AI-specific sandbox
quote: Runtime defense is the set of features that provide both predictive and threat-based active protection for running containers.
notes: Defender runtime defense (process, network, filesystem models) applies to any container or host, including AI workloads. The EE AI-SPM section has no AI/ML sandboxing or isolation feature. The dash icon stands.

param: Prevent Public Exposure of AI Models & Datasets
pc_new: AI-SPM detects public model endpoints and sensitive training data; detection, not blocking
quote: AI-SPM detects that the model's API endpoints are publicly accessible without authentication
notes: Blog dated Aug 6 2024 (AI-SPM GA). AI-SPM overview tracks Model Endpoints, Inference Datasets, Training Datasets and Plugins, with default and custom risk rules. Supported services in EE docs: AWS Bedrock Provisioned Throughput and Bedrock Agent, Azure OpenAI Deployment, GCP Vertex Endpoint, unmanaged models (https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/ai-security-posture-management/aispmassets). SageMaker is not listed. Enforcement runs through alerts and remediation integrations. The dash icon stands.

pc_new: UEBA anomaly policies alert on unusual user locations; no AI-model-specific geo policy
quote: Prisma Cloud detects deviations from typical user behavior, by profiling users’ console and API activities to identify types of cloud services accessed and accessed locations.
notes: Resolves the contradiction: the live cell has a tick icon but 'Limited' text. The evidence supports Limited, so the icon should be a dash. Account hijacking policies cover impossible time travel and logins from unknown locations. Some UEBA login policies ingest AWS login activity only. The AI-SPM pages list no geo or region access alert for models.

pc_new: Native push to Splunk HEC, Amazon Security Lake (OCSF), webhooks, SQS, Azure Service Bus
quote: Prisma® Cloud integrates with Splunk and monitors your assets and sends alerts for resource misconfigurations, compliance violations, network security risks, and anomalous user activities to Splunk.
notes: The EE integration list has no native Sentinel or QRadar integration. Microsoft publishes a Sentinel connector for Prisma Cloud CSPM that pulls from the Prisma API (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors/palo-alto-prisma-cloud-cspm). Runtime (Defender) events also go to syslog and stdout. DSPM alerts go out through SNS, webhooks and Torq, not to Splunk directly.

pc_new: Jira and ServiceNow are push integrations; alert state changes update tickets one way
quote: When you dismiss an alert on Prisma Cloud, Prisma Cloud sends a state change notification to update the ticket status on ServiceNow.
notes: Same page: 'Manually changing the incident will stop notifications from being sent.' The docs show no reverse sync from the ticket back to the alert. The Supported Capabilities table lists Jira and ServiceNow as 'Push' (https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/administration/configure-external-integrations-on-prisma-cloud/integrations-feature-support). Jira templates can push Open and Resolved states. The tick icon should be a dash.
